A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLIE framework. All 19 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Local reporting inconsistencies are noted in the affected judgments.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Tables 1–2 report original classification experiments comparing RLIE, baselines, and inference strategies across six benchmark tasks.

after.justification: Tables 1–7 report original classification, computational-cost, rule-evolution, sensitivity, and calibration results, including experiments documented in Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes capacity-based rule pruning from ranking individual validation accuracy to ranking validation F1, additionally specifying non-abstaining samples. This modifies rule selection within the retained framework; ternary judgments, Elastic Net logistic regression, hard-example refinement, and the four inference strategies remain.

E1.justification: The six benchmark columns remain, and added analyses reuse these tasks. However, v1 describes Dreddit/Dreaddit as pairwise argument persuasion, while v2 describes stress detection from Reddit posts; v2 Appendix A.3 still retains the persuasion heading. The PDFs do not establish whether actual task coverage changed or an earlier description was corrected.

E2.justification: Section 4.2 and Table 1 add Few-shot (ICL) as an evaluated comparator. Zero-shot Inference, Zero-shot Generation, IO Refinement, and HypoGeniC remain, with shortened names for the zero-shot methods. Backbone substitutions are experimental-setting changes.

E3.justification: The reported setup changes from GPT-4o-mini and 200/200/300 samples to DeepSeek-V3.2, additional Qwen backbones, and original HypoBench splits described as full datasets. Appendix C adds ten-bin ECE evaluation and constrained single-token prompting with token probabilities. Exact split and tuning procedures remain inconsistent: Appendix A.2 retains 200-sample language, while Appendix A.4 places cross-validation on training data although Section 3.2 still specifies validation data.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained inference-strategy comparison, v2 adds computational-cost analysis, a Retweets rule-evolution case study, Headlines rule embeddings and learned-rule inspection, coverage-threshold sensitivity, and calibration analysis (Sections 5.3–5.4 and Appendices B–C). These test efficiency, refinement behavior, representation, sensitivity, and confidence reliability that v1 did not empirically analyze.

E5.justification: v1 reports means and standard deviations throughout Tables 1–2 and states at least three repetitions. v2 specifies three runs with different seeds but removes standard deviations from both main tables; mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting appears in calibration Table 7. This substantially reduces uncertainty reporting for the primary comparisons. An increase in run count is not established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace the GPT-4o-mini results with DeepSeek/Qwen results under revised settings, so numerical differences are not same-setting performance gains. Tables 3–7 add costs, rule weights and trajectories, sensitivity scores, and ECE results favoring RLIE on five of six tasks. v2 also contains a result inconsistency: Qwen3-Next Headlines Accuracy/F1 is 61.1/60.9 in Table 1 but 62.9/62.7 in Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation of ternary rule features, logistic aggregation, Elastic Net learning, coverage, and hard-example selection is substantively retained. Neither version provides theoretical proofs or theorems. v2's standard ECE formula and calibration motivation add empirical explanation rather than new mathematical results.

C1.justification: The central claim favoring LLM semantic judgments combined with external probabilistic aggregation remains. v2 broadens the abstract and conclusion to multiple LLM backbones, qualifies rule-injection outcomes as mixed and often detrimental, and foregrounds hard-example refinement in the contribution list.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations attributing token savings to hard-example refinement, weight trajectories to soft feature selection, embedding patterns to semantic efficiency or comparator mode collapse, and ECE differences to reduced overconfidence. These explanations accompany new analyses. Conversely, v1's pretraining-leakage caveat and detailed graphical/Bayesian extension discussion are removed or substantially reduced.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.4 documents scikit-learn, a 30-by-30 regularization grid, five-fold cross-validation, 20 maximum iterations, patience 3, improvement threshold 0.001, and an 8000-token limit. v2 also documents token accounting and the assumed energy conversion. It removes v1's explicit commitments to release code and exact splits. The seven Retweets prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Guo et al. (2017) for calibration and omits the Liu et al. (2025) HypoBench reference, although HypoBench remains named. Section 2.2 drops v1's explicit claim to be the first to combine LLMs with probabilistic weighted-rule learning. The broader positioning relative to classical and LLM-based rule learning remains.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition, results interpretation, discussion, and conclusion. It reorganizes the contribution narrative and replaces the ethics/reproducibility sections with an Impact Statement. The retained LLM-usage and prompt appendices move from B/C to D/E.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two columns. Tables 1–2 are redesigned around paired Accuracy/F1 entries and backbone groups. v2 adds an aggregation illustration, a t-SNE plot, and Tables 3–7. The original pipeline graphic is retained and enlarged as Figure 2; prompt displays are reformatted and redistributed.

improvement.justification: v2 makes previously asserted calibration and rule-compactness properties more assessable through Appendix C and concrete rule studies, broadens backbone evaluation, and supplies missing tuning details. These provide a limited net improvement. However, removing main-table standard deviations, conflicting split and cross-validation descriptions, and inconsistent Qwen3-Next Headlines scores weaken confidence in the expanded evidence and limit the overall gain.
